content.title: 2026 Process Improvements
content.summary: The Arvada Building Safety Division is enhancing transparency and efficiency in its permitting and inspection processes to better serve the community. Recent improvements include the establishment of a formal online process for requesting alternative materials and methods, as well as significant changes to streamline residential permit applications, thereby reducing review times and documentation requirements for new construction projects. These updates aim to support innovation while maintaining essential safety standards in building codes.
content.body:
The Arvada Building Safety Division is continuously working to improve transparency, efficiency, communication, and customer service for our community. Over the past year, our team has been actively reviewing internal processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, updating resources, and implementing changes intended to help projects move through the permitting and inspection process more successfully.

As our community continues to grow and construction methods, products, and codes continue to evolve, our goal is to create processes that are clearer, more predictable, and more supportive, while still maintaining the important life safety standards established by the adopted building codes.

Below are some of the recent updates, clarifications, and process improvements currently underway within the Building Safety Division.

## May 2026

1. [Alternative materials and methods and code modification requests](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_0)

One of the biggest updates we have recently made is the **creation of a formal online process for requesting:**

- Alternative materials and methods approvals
- Design alternatives
- Code modification requests

While these requests have always been allowed under the building code, they were historically handled through a more informal process when unique situations arose during plan review or inspections.

**Our goal with this update is to create greater transparency, consistency, and awareness surrounding these important code provisions.**

The building code is intentionally designed to allow innovation, evolving technology, unique building products, and alternative construction methods — provided that the proposed solution can demonstrate that it still meets the intent of the code and does not lessen health, life safety, fire safety, accessibility, or structural performance.

**In simple terms: if you can demonstrate that a different product, material, design, engineering approach, or construction method achieves an equivalent level of code compliance and safety, there may be a pathway for our team to review and consider that option.**

Additionally, the updated process now clearly explains how modification requests may be considered in situations where there are practical difficulties in carrying out the strict letter of the code. While the Building Safety Division cannot waive code requirements, the code does provide the Building Official with limited authority to consider modifications on a case-by-case basis when special circumstances exist and the proposed solution still aligns with the intent and purpose of the code without reducing safety protections.

We believe making these processes more visible and accessible will help encourage collaboration, support innovation, reduce confusion, and provide our community with a better understanding of the flexibility and options that already exist within the code framework.

1. [Ongoing improvements to residential permit processes](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_1)

Over the past year, the Building Safety Division has been actively working to significantly reduce plan review timeframes and simplify the permitting process for new single-family homes, townhomes, and duplex projects.

One of the largest changes we have made involved restructuring which documents are required for master permits versus repeat site-specific permits associated with approved master plans. **By shifting the majority of required documentation to the master permit review stage, we have been able to:**

- Reduce repeat permit plan review times
- Reduce the number of documents applicants must repeatedly submit
- Streamline the application process for repeat permits
- Improve overall review consistency and efficiency

An additional benefit of this transition has been allowing documents such as Manual J, D, and S calculations and energy compliance documentation to be approved at the master permit stage rather than requiring them to be site-specific for every permit. This change has created meaningful cost savings and reduced administrative burdens for our building community.

Our team is continuing to work on additional improvements later in 2026, including:

- Further reducing repeat permit review timeframes
- Evaluating the removal of repeat plan review fees for qualifying permits
- Updating Certificate of Occupancy checklists and expectations
- Improving pre-construction meeting formats, resources, and guidance
- Reviewing how master permits are submitted and processed to create a more efficient experience
- Expanding handouts, checklists, and educational resources to provide clearer expectations earlier in the process

We want projects to move forward successfully and in alignment with project timelines, and we believe that clearer expectations and stronger guidance upfront help create a smoother process for everyone involved.

1. [Additional process improvements and permit review changes](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_2)

As part of our ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and reduce unnecessary review timelines, the Building Safety Division has continued**evaluating which permit types require formal plan review and where opportunities exist to simplify processes while still maintaining important safety protections.**

Effective June 1, 2026, residential permits for the following projects **will no longer require a formal building plan review prior to permit issuance:**

- Electric Vehicle (EV) Chargers
- Solar Systems
- Residential Battery Backup / Energy Storage Systems (ESS)
- Bay Windows
- Above ground hot tubs and spas

These changes are part of a larger effort to reduce unnecessary review steps, shorten permit processing timelines, and allow staff to focus review efforts on higher-risk or more complex projects.

Our goal with this change is to help reduce permit processing timelines and allow qualifying residential projects to move forward more efficiently. However, permit applicants, contractors, and property owners remain responsible for complying with all adopted codes, manufacturer installation requirements, and approved product listing requirements.

**We strongly encourage applicants and contractors to review all code requirements and the guidance and resources available on our website prior to beginning work in order to avoid delays, corrections, or added costs during inspections. This guidance and the resources we are providing is not a complete list of all requirements, so it is important to plan for all code requirements and be prepared for them.**

1. [Foundation-only permit process improvements](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_3)

The Building Safety Division is continuing to evaluate and improve our foundation-only permit process for new residential single-family homes, townhomes, and duplex projects.

Over the past year, the City of Arvada expanded the use of foundation-only permits for these residential project types. This phased permitting approach was created to help projects continue moving forward while applicants work through additional requirements such as warranty review processes, Right-of-Way permits, and coordination with Engineering and Public Works.

**Staff is currently working on:**

- Website updates and application guidance
- Clear expectations for permit issuance and inspections
- Process improvements
- Guidance for closing out foundation-only permits and transitioning into vertical site permits
- Updated pre-construction meeting resources related to phased permits

**We will continue refining this process throughout 2026 and encourage applicants to monitor our website for future updates and guidance.**

1. [Disaster assessment and emergency preparedness planning](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_4)

The Arvada Building Safety Division is currently developing its first formal disaster assessment process and emergency response framework.

In the event of a disaster or emergency, Building Safety staff play a critical role in evaluating structures for safety and determining whether occupancy can continue or if buildings pose a risk to the public. These efforts are coordinated alongside many other City departments, emergency responders, and volunteer organizations.

Our team is actively working to develop a formal framework for post-disaster building evaluations, occupancy safety assessments, emergency coordination and staff training so that Arvada is better prepared and more resilient in the future.

While much of this work happens behind the scenes, it is an important part of ensuring the long-term safety and resiliency of our community.

1. [Commercial tenant finish, change of use, and occupancy process updates](#tab2f743192-d2f3-41d2-b075-35d118d85268_5)

**The Building Safety Division is also currently evaluating and updating processes related to:**

- Commercial tenant finishes
- Change of use permits
- Change of occupancy reviews
- Certificate of Occupancy requirements for businesses

One common misconception is that permits are only required when construction work is being performed. However, there are situations where a business may move into an existing space without performing construction, but a permit or review may still be required in order to establish a proper Certificate of Occupancy for the new use.

When a business changes the use or occupancy classification of a space, the applicable building, fire, accessibility, plumbing, mechanical, and electrical code requirements may also change depending on how the building will function and operate.

**Our team is currently working on improving guidance, resources, and communication related to these processes so businesses have clearer expectations and a better understanding of when permits or reviews may be required.**

For additional information, updated guidance, and future process updates, please continue monitoring the Building Safety Division website.

As always, please reach out to us if you have any questions about this process and what might be required for any future projects or businesses moving into new spaces.
